summary: Skagit County lookout site: a 1933 CCC-era tower, replaced by a DNR tower in 1958-59 and destroyed in 1981; no source describes the site today, and access is restricted.

facts.design: 55-foot pole tower with 8x8 foot cab (first tower); 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower (replacement)
facts.status_note: The 40-foot DNR tower was destroyed in 1981; no source read describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: last documented season: October 1956 (Maxine Meyers); Aircraft Warning Service observers 1942-1943

access.note: Final road to the summit crosses private timberland, where access is usually blocked at the boundary (WillhiteWeb). The DNR temporarily closed Harry Osborne State Forest to vehicle access in May 2023 (KIRO 7); no source read says whether that closure is still in place.

visit.trail_note: Walk from as high as a vehicle can get; WillhiteWeb gives a hiking distance of probably 2.5 miles. The road hike on the back side is part of the Pacific Northwest Trail.

events.note: Washington Forest Fire Association worked with the CCC to erect a 55-foot pole tower with an 8x8 cab (Forest Lookouts, WillhiteWeb)
Firetower.org and firelookout.com date the first 55-foot tower to 1938
Aircraft Warning Service used the tower to spot aircraft; activated March 8, 1942
Aircraft Warning Service document lists Harry Osborne as warden in 1943, with two observers
Maxine Meyers of Lyman worked alone through October 1956 after a man did not finish the season
DNR replaced the original tower with a 40-foot wooden live-in tower (WillhiteWeb dates it to 1958; firetower.org and firelookout.com to 1959)
DNR announced a temporary closure of Harry Osborne State Forest to vehicle access (May 2023); walk-in recreation stayed open

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb say the Washington Forest Fire Association and the CCC put up the tower in 1933. Firetower.org and firelookout.com say the first lookout was built in 1938. The story reports both dates.
WillhiteWeb dates the DNR replacement to 1958; firetower.org and firelookout.com date it to 1959. Forest Lookouts gives a 1958-60 range for the DNR crew's lookouts.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes what remains at the summit today, so the story says so. The access section is from WillhiteWeb, whose maps it says were good for 2020. The May 2023 DNR closure comes from one news report (KIRO 7); the goSkagit copy returned HTTP 429 and was not read, and no DNR notice was read, so current status is unknown. Historic Forest Lookouts data also includes a National Geodetic Survey description with gate and key details from 1939 and 1950; it was left out as dated. Firetower.org and firelookout.com agree the replacement was destroyed in 1981, but the cause is not in any source read.
